title: Operational stability cadence and safety net plan
summary: High-level plan to create a predictable operational cadence and safety-net for model-serving services across product teams. Focus: create cross-team rituals, define guardrail checks, and tie SLOs to actionable runbooks and error-budget responses.
background: Recent outages and noisy degradation during model rollouts highlighted gaps in cross-team coordination: inconsistent runbook ownership, unclear error-budget responses, and no lightweight escalation matrix for degraded tail latency. This doc sketches a pragmatic, low-friction program to reduce incident-to-recovery time and prevent quality regressions by linking SLO signals to concrete playbooks and a simple cadence of check-ins.
goals: Establish a repeatable weekly operational cadence for critical model-serving endpoints
Define typed responses for three error-budget tiers and map playbooks to each
Onboard three pilot product teams with runbooks and tabletop exercises by end of Q1 2027
Create a compact SLO scorecard and automate a subset of remediation actions
success_criteria: Mean time to restore (MTTR) for tier-1 incidents reduced by 30% within two quarters
At least 80% of SLO breaches trigger the mapped playbook within 15 minutes
Pilot teams adopt the cadence and record tabletop completion in the shared tracker
Automated mitigation handles >50% of high-frequency transient latency spikes
approach_overview: Use a phased rollout: discovery, playbook authoring, small pilot rollouts with automated alerts and action hooks, followed by broader adoption. Focus on lightweight artifacts (one-page runbooks, an error-budget dashboard, and a weekly 30-minute stability standup) so teams can adopt without heavy ceremony.
milestones: Discovery sprint (2 weeks): inventory SLOs, current runbooks, and alert noise across candidate services - target 2026-11-19
Playbook templates and error-budget tiers published: 2026-12-03
Instrumentation sprint to wire SLO scorecard and alert hooks (2 sprints): 2026-12-04 to 2027-01-21
Pilot onboarding (3 teams): tabletop + 30-day live experiment: start 2027-02-01
roles_and_responsibilities: SRE lead (Aisha Kumar): program owner, overall coordination, metrics
Product reliability liaisons (one per pilot team - Daniel Park, Lina Torres, Priya Shah): own team runbooks and facilitate tabletop exercises
Observability engineer (Marco Ruiz): build SLO scorecard, automate alert hooks and dashboards
Incident commander rota owners (eng platform): implement cross-team oncall rotation for severity-1 breaches
Solutions engineering: validate safety-net behaviors for Dedicated and Private deployments
error_budget_tiers_and_actions: Tier 1 (critical): immediate incident channel, full runbook, page SRE-IC, rollback or fallback to stable model variant
Tier 2 (degrading): notify product liaison and SRE on-call, enable traffic limiters, enable graceful degradation features, run targeted mitigation script
Tier 3 (observability/noise): flagged for next-day triage, adjust alert thresholds and investigate false positives
measurement_plan: Primary metrics: SLO attainment percentage, MTTR, error-budget burn rate (1h/24h windows)
Secondary metrics: alert fatigue score (alerts per engineer per week), number of automated mitigations executed
Dashboards: per-service SLO scorecard, cross-team latency tail percentiles, recent runbook activations
communication_plan: Weekly 30-minute Stability Standup: 10-min updates per pilot, 10-min signal review, 10-min blockers - Tuesdays 09:00 PT
Monthly reliability newsletter: highlights, recent runbook activations, learnings
Incident postmortems and short 'what-we-changed' notes published to the cross-functional channel
meeting_rhythm: Kickoff working session (90m) with pilot teams - week of 2026-11-22
Weekly playbook-authoring office hours (60m) - Thursdays 11:00 PT
Quarterly executive check-in to review program KPIs and resourcing needs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Teams view this as additional process overhead - Mitigation: keep artifacts one page, emphasize automation and remove manual triage where possible
Risk: Alert noise drowns out signal - Mitigation: dedicate an observability sprint to suppress false positives and tune thresholds before pilot
Risk: Rollback/fallback options may not be available for all model variants - Mitigation: product teams to prioritize a 'stable variant' contract for mission-critical routes
pilot_selection_criteria: Service exposes public latency-sensitive endpoints and has >5k QPS per day
Team has an identified product liaison and is open to running tabletop exercises
Clear SLOs or metrics already being collected (even if immature)
next_steps: Schedule discovery sprint planning meeting and invite pilot team liaisons (action: Aisha) - by 2026-11-02
Create playbook authoring template and a Google Doc starter for each pilot (action: Daniel) - by 2026-11-05
Open observability sprint tickets and allocate one FTE for dashboarding (action: Marco) - by 2026-11-08
notes_to_reviewers: This is intentionally light on formal process—feedback welcome on whether the cadence is realistic for product teams. Looking for two pilot teams and one platform partner to sign up before we commit to the instrumentation sprint.
